title: autoformat-label-notify and copilot-review: keep the run-scoped concurrency group when trigger events do different work
answers: Why does copilot-review.yml keep a run-scoped concurrency group instead of a PR-level one?
Why was the autoformat label notification workflow not grouped per PR?
Should a new workflow triggered by several label or review events share a PR-level concurrency group?
body:
Path: the concurrency block in .github/workflows/autoformat-label-notify.yml (fires on any `labeled` event) and .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml (fires on `opened`, `ready_for_review` and `review_requested`), the two pull_request_target workflows that stay outside the PR-scoped group.
Rule: when a workflow's trigger types do different things, and most runs are no-ops for the job-level `if:`, use `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` so each run is its own group and no run can displace another. A PR-level group would let a no-op run (an unrelated label, or a review_requested on a non-draft PR) replace a pending run that had work to do.
Constraints: chosen because these workflows fire rarely, so grouping buys little. Keying the group on label name or event action was considered and rejected as a compound key not worth its complexity. Does not apply to the PR-scoped workflows where every triggering event does the same job.
applies: Choosing a concurrency group for a pull_request_target workflow whose trigger types or job conditions differ.
says: Automated code review comments fail to trigger when multiple pull request events happen.
Formatting notification comments on pull requests get cancelled by unrelated label changes.
Prevent pending pull request automation runs from being cancelled by no-op events.
Automated review requests get skipped when subsequent review actions arrive simultaneously.
search: Workflow concurrency configuration in .github/workflows/autoformat-label-notify.yml and .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml must use run-scoped concurrency groups via github.run_id instead of pull request-level groups. This prevents no-op trigger events, such as unrelated labels or review requests on non-draft pull requests, from cancelling pending runs that have active work. Applies to pull_request_target workflows whose trigger types or job conditions perform differing tasks, and does not apply to workflows where every trigger executes identical jobs.
